section_1.title: The Prerequisites: Motion and Change
section_1.content: Establish the foundation by reviewing the concepts of 'Rate of Change' (Derivative) and 'Total Accumulation' (Integral). Introduce 'Dash the Cheetah' to illustrate movement. Explain that if we know position, we can find speed; if we know speed, can we find position?
section_1.example: Visualize Dash the Cheetah running across a savannah. A graph shows his Position (y) vs. Time (x). The 'steepness' of his path at any moment is his velocity.

section_2.title: The Derivative: Zooming into the Slope
section_2.content: Focus on the derivative as the instantaneous rate of change. Use a magnifying glass animation to zoom into a curve until it looks like a straight line. Define the derivative f'(x) as the slope of the tangent line.
section_2.example: As Dash runs, the slope of his position graph at t=2 seconds shows exactly how fast his speedometer reads at that instant (e.g., 25 m/s).

section_3.title: The Integral: Accumulating the Area
section_3.content: Shift focus to the velocity graph. Introduce the definite integral as the 'Area Under the Curve.' Explain that multiplying 'speed' (height) by 'time' (width) gives 'distance.' Use an animation of a color-filling 'paint roller' moving across the graph.
section_3.example: Dash's velocity varies over time. The shaded area under his velocity-time graph from t=0 to t=5 represents the total meters he has traveled in those 5 seconds.

section_4.title: The Bridge: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
section_4.content: Show the visual 'magic.' Define an Area Function A(x). Demonstrate that as we increase the area by a tiny sliver (dx), the rate at which the area grows is exactly the height of the function at 그 point. This proves that the derivative of the integral is the original function.
section_4.example: A thin rectangular 'sliver' of area is added to Dash's distance graph. The height of this sliver is his current velocity. Therefore, the rate of change of 'Total Distance' is 'Current Velocity.'

section_5.title: Inverse Operations: The Mathematical U-Turn
section_5.content: Solidify the concept that integration and differentiation are inverse processes, much like addition and subtraction. Present the 'Calculus Loop' animation: start with Position, differentiate to get Velocity, integrate to return to Position.
section_5.example: A 'Time Machine' device: Input Dash's velocity function, press the 'Integrate' button to output his position. Input his position, press 'Differentiate' to see his velocity again.

section_6.title: Summary and Practical Application
section_6.content: Summarize the 5-minute journey. Reiterate that the derivative breaks a whole into tiny rates, while the integral assembles tiny parts into a whole. Mention real-world uses like calculating fuel consumption or satellite orbits.
section_6.example: Final split-screen: On the left, a car's speedometer (Derivative); on the right, the car's odometer (Integral). They are two sides of the same coin.

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
